attributes.value: Under the regional Toscana IGT designation, this cuvée bridges Italian tradition and international ambition. Brilliant with Beefsteak Fiorentina or pasta with Bolognese sauce.

attributes.value: Alexandre Gendrier met Paulina during a trip to Quebec in 2007. Since then, she has worked with him at Domaine des Huards, owned by the family since 1846. Gradually taking over the reins of the operation, their mission remains the same: the integrity of the wines. No product resulting from synthetic chemistry is used and the fermentations are carried out with natural yeasts. Fine, elegant and with bright fruit, this successful marriage between Pinot and Gamay is incredibly satisfying paired to barbecue-grilled salmon or a beef tartar.

attributes.name: argumentaire_vente_externe
attributes.value: Developed by Ernesto Catena, a name that no longer needs an introduction in the Argentinian wine world, this is a great cuvée that will appeal to lovers of rather concentrated wines. With a supple tannic structure, it will please fans of the typical New-World style wines. Pair with lamb chops or a good Lac Saint-Jean tourtière!

attributes.name: argumentaire_vente_externe
attributes.value: This wine showcases Pinot Noir, a grape less common in the region, yet celebrated for its refined aromas of cherry, raspberry, and subtle floral and spicy notes. Its silky texture and delicate tannins make it a pleasure to enjoy. This is a graceful, approachable red that pairs just as well with a generously topped pizza as it does with roasted white meats or a platter of fine cheeses.

attributes.name: argumentaire_vente_externe
attributes.value: Once again, Italy offers us a bottle that turns heads. Delicate and light, this white from the Soave appellation is very dry with aromas of white fruit and vegetal notes. Another great choice as an aperitif or to put on your checkered blanket alongside a salad or a shrimp, pesto and goat cheese pizza.

attributes.value: Fresh, fruity and easy-drinking is usually what you expect from a regional Beaujolais appellation. However, Les Griottes cuvee from the duo Pierre-Marie and Martine Chermette is rather colourful and showcases plenty of substance. Made from the youngest vines of the estate, it offers ripe fruit, floral and licorice notes in a full and tight.

attributes.name: argumentaire_vente_externe
attributes.value: By far the most popular alcohol-free wine and even among the best sellers among traditional wines, this cuvée produced by the famous Torres house in Spain delivers all the exuberant side of the Muscat grape. Its notes of elderflower, orange blossoms and fresh grapes appeal to both aperitifs and Asian dishes. Fruity and sweet, a touch of residual sugar characterizes it and contributes to giving it the classic touch of a regular wine.

attributes.name: argumentaire_vente_externe
attributes.value: When talking about classics, it's hard to ignore Bordeaux. This Pessac-Léognan from Pierre Lurton is definitely one of the must-buys in the regular catalogue, with a length and overall balance that make it a standout.
